features.text: The patient is a 32-year-old male.
The patient injured his right knee three days ago while playing soccer.
The patient experiences swelling in his right knee.
The patient has difficulty moving his right knee as it used to.
The patient experiences pain in his right knee.
The patient cannot fully bend or straighten his right knee without discomfort.
The patient describes the injury as a sudden pop on the inside of his right knee.
The patient did not twist his knee or collide with another player during the injury.
The patient has not experienced instability or the knee giving way since the injury.
The patient does not have a prior history of knee issues, surgeries, or chronic conditions.
The patient has not undergone any imaging studies for this injury.
The patient will have an MRI ordered to check the integrity of his ACL after this visit.
The patient describes the pop as occurring on the inside of his right knee.
The patient did not hear any specific sound at the time of injury.
The patient describes the injury as feeling like something gave way when making the movement.
The patient rates his current pain as a 6 or 7 on a scale from 1 to 10.
The patient experiences discomfort while walking.
The patient can still walk on the injured knee but finds it uncomfortable.
The patient experiences tenderness on the inside of his right knee.
The patient has difficulty sitting for long periods or moving his leg without discomfort.
The patient has not noticed any clicking, popping, or locking sensations in his knee.
The patient has not experienced any numbness or tingling in his leg.
The patient has not had any previous episodes of knee instability or injury.
The patient was attempting a plank kick when the injury occurred.
The patient did not have contact with another player during the injury.
The patient describes the injury as happening quickly when making the movement.
The patient has not experienced any numbness or tingling in his leg since the injury.
The patient describes the tenderness as being on the inside of his knee, near the joint line.
The patient notes that the swelling has been decreasing over the past three days.
The patient still experiences instability and weakness in his knee, especially when moving it fully.
The patient experiences worsening instability and weakness when bending or straightening the knee.
The patient has to use his hand to help straighten the knee sometimes.
The patient notes that the swelling has decreased slightly over the past few days.
The patient still experiences a feeling of looseness and instability in the knee.
